analysis.title: From Druckenmiller's Chip Dump To Aschenbrenner's $18.7 Billion Vanishing Act: What The "Smart Money" Was Doing Right Before The AI Trade Blew Up
key_insights: Q3 13F filings (Sept. 30 snapshot, filed Nov. 16) show three of four chip-heavy hedge fund books were cutting semiconductor exposure before the Nov. 5 selloff, one (Tepper) was adding, and Nvidia was selling part of its Intel stake. Of ten filers, seven reported a smaller 13F book at end-September than at end-June.

Druckenmiller's Duquesne cut TSMC 94% (589,680 to 32,700 ADS, $282M to $15M), halved STMicro, and sold AMD, Sandisk, Lam Research, Arm, Entegris, Rambus, Qnity and Navitas. Chip and storage names fell from 16% to 10% of the book. Seagate is most of what is left, nearly tripled to $315M plus $90M of calls. He opened a $129M gold-miner trio (Newmont, Barrick, Agnico Eagle).

Lone Pine rotated rather than reduced. It cut Applied Materials 92%, ASML 25%, Teradyne and Seagate, sold Corning and TTM outright, and cut Nebius 64%, Hut 8 67% and TeraWulf 56%. It bought TSMC (101,242 ADS to 1.72M, $783M) and a new $721M Intel position. Core chip holdings were $2.72B at Sept. 30 vs $2.78B at June 30, so exposure was roughly unchanged. Bloomberg reported the Cypress fund up 44% through June, up 0.6% through September, and down another 8.8% in October.

Tepper's Appaloosa was the one chip buyer. Micron rose 28% to 1.25M shares ($1.33B, the largest position), Nvidia rose 31% to 2M shares, Lam Research and ASML were added and Applied Materials opened. Chips went from 35% to 39% of the book. He trimmed Alphabet 46% and Meta 22% and multiplied SpaceX 17x to $557M. Micron and Lam each fell about 17% in one session five weeks later.

Situational Awareness (Aschenbrenner) reported $1.58B of 13F positions at Sept. 30 vs $20.24B at June 30, a $18.7B (92%) drop. Twenty-one of 26 lines were closed, including $5.67B Sandisk, $5.57B Micron, $1.90B Bloom Energy, $1.27B TSMC and $1.23B Nebius. The article says levered bets failed in late July, the book was sold to Citadel at a reported 10% discount, and the fund re-built similar trades by September.

Two-thirds of Situational Awareness's remaining reported value is call options, including Bloom Energy calls (145,800 to 1.4M underlying shares), Nebius calls and a memory ETF. Its largest stock position is SharonAI, raised 50% to 8.07M shares worth $441M. The article frames this as the fund returning to leveraged options on AI momentum names going into October.

Intel was the consensus Q3 long. Soros Fund Management raised its stake from 100,000 to 2.83M shares ($340M, its largest stock holding) and Lone Pine bought $721M new. Nvidia sold, cutting its Intel position from 214.8M to 161.1M shares, about $6.5B at quarter-end prices, more than the roughly $5B it reportedly paid for the stake. Nvidia also cut Nokia 56% and Synopsys 10%, added SpaceX (now its largest holding at $19.68B), and its 13F book fell 24% to $48.3B. The article says Intel has lost about half its value in recent months.
SpaceX split the crowd. Tepper went up 17x, Druckenmiller opened a small position and Nvidia added 6%, while BlueCrest sold 94% of its stake ($242M to $13M).

Macro funds: Soros's largest line is puts on the Energy Select SPDR (2M to 10.9M underlying shares, $670M notional) plus $328M of new puts on the oil and gas E&P ETF, about $1B notional against an $8.5B reported book. It also bought calls on long Treasuries (TLT, $237M) and utilities (XLU, $215M). The article says energy puts aged well after the midterms removed oil's war premium.

BlueCrest sold index ETFs and rebuilt exposure through options. S&P 500 calls went from 30,000 to 850,000 underlying shares ($648M notional, 23% of the reported book). It also raised puts on HYG, XLF and IWM and bought TLT calls, a long-index, short-credit and short-small-cap structure.

Non-chip filers were calmer. Berkshire bought Bending Spoons ($689M), nearly doubled Lennar to $2.17B combined, cut Bank of America by 27.5M shares (about $1.5B), left Apple at 25% of the book, and reportedly holds $377B in cash. Pershing Square bought $1B each of Intercontinental Exchange and Alcon, funded by cutting Microsoft 35%. Its 21% book increase is mostly Pershing Square Inc. shares rising on price. Einhorn raised PG&E to 10M shares.

PG&E was added by four of ten filers (Einhorn, Tepper, BlueCrest via calls on 4.5M shares, Soros via a 27% increase in convertible notes to $219M), which the article calls the closest thing to a non-AI consensus trade in the sample.

Across 19 filers, megacaps were mixed: Amazon seven buyers and seven sellers, Meta seven buyers and five sellers, Alphabet five buyers and eight sellers. Cleaner reads were Intel (five buyers, one seller: Nvidia), Micron (four buyers, Situational Awareness the only exit), and Broadcom and Nebius (no buyers, three sellers).

Goldman prime brokerage data cited by the article puts the US Info Tech long/short ratio at 1.5, the lowest since 2016, with hedge funds more than 20 points underweight the sector vs the S&P. Goldman estimates tech-focused long/short funds were up 24% at the June peak and back to roughly flat after Nov. 5, with high-beta TMT momentum stocks down 56% after rising 125% through Q2.

The article argues the de-risking began before October. Druckenmiller was out of most chips by September and Situational Awareness by August. October and Nov. 5 hurt funds that rotated rather than reduced (Lone Pine) and funds that added (Tepper). It expects the February 13Fs to show more names in the red columns.
Limits of the data: 13Fs show US-listed longs and options (calls and puts carried at underlying value) only, with no shorts, swaps, bonds or Korean memory stocks, and are stale by roughly 45 days.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds cut chip exposure ahead of the Nov. 5 selloff, and the article expects further losses to show up in February filings. It also notes the record-low tech long/short ratio could set up a squeeze.
Soros held about $1B of notional puts on XLE and an E&P ETF after the midterms removed oil's war premium.
Four of ten filers added to PG&E, and Soros bought XLU calls ($215M).

crypto_views: Lone Pine sold most of its AI-power and bitcoin-miner holdings: Nebius down 64%, Hut 8 down 67%, TeraWulf down 56%.
Soros Capital cut TeraWulf (WULF) to 22K from 762K shares. Intel's corporate book opened a new IREN position of 1.29M shares.
Miller Value Partners raised MicroStrategy (MSTR) to 61K from 50K shares.
risk_factors: The article expects the February 13F round to show more funds in the red columns after the Nov. 5 semiconductor drop.
Funds that rotated within chips (Lone Pine) or added (Tepper) took losses in October and Nov. 5, and leveraged options exposure persists at Situational Awareness.
Soros holds TLT and XLU calls while the article says the Fed is hiking.
13F data omits shorts, swaps and non-US holdings and is about 45 days old, so it may not reflect current positioning.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman prime brokerage: US Info Tech long/short ratio at 1.5, the lowest in its records back to 2016, with hedge funds more than 20 points underweight the sector vs the S&P.
Goldman's traders called the recent de-risking the biggest degross since Covid. John Flood told Reuters funds were selling hyperscalers they had bought a day earlier.
JPMorgan estimates October cost hedge funds 3%. Goldman estimates tech-focused long/short funds went from +24% at the June peak to roughly flat after Nov. 5, for about -1% YTD.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 12.25% on Nov. 5, described as the Nasdaq's worst day since Covid.

tension_points.bull_case: Bulls say a record-low tech long/short ratio (1.5, lowest since 2016) with hedge funds more than 20 points underweight is what a washed-out market looks like and sets up a large short squeeze.
tension_points.bear_case: The filings show the fund that blew up in July was back in leveraged calls by September, the largest chip long in the sample (Tepper) was increasing into the crash, and Nvidia, the seller with the best view of AI demand, was cutting Intel. The article expects more names in the red columns in the next 13Fs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The February 13F filings: the article's bear view is that they will show more funds in the red columns.
